newsitem.title: ETHIOPIA: Ethiopia wants Kenyan help to stop clan fighting.
newsitem.headline: Ethiopia wants Kenyan help to stop clan fighting.

text.p: An Ethiopian government official has said that Kenya and Ethiopia must set up a system to prevent conflicts between border clans after up to 80 people died in recent fighting.
Tekeda Alemu, deputy foreign minister, told a meeting of the Ethiopia-Kenya Joint Border Commission in Addis Ababa that casualties were likely whenever clashes took place.

Tekeda's comments, carried by state Ethiopia Television on Wednesday, were the first Ethiopian government reaction to clan fighting along the Kenyan-Ethiopian border last week in which as many as 80 people were killed, including 19 Kenyan policemen.
Kenya sent troops and the paramilitary General Service Unit to affected areas and President Daniel arap Moi said he would sent a protest note to Ethiopia.
Kenyan police said Ethiopian clan fighters crossed into Kenya, butchered innocent villagers and stole 4,000 cattle. Ethiopia made no comment.

"Ethiopia and Kenya must set up a mechanism that would ensure tranquility and peace along their common border," Tekeda was quoted as saying. He praised the good neighbourliness between the two countries.
The television did not give a Kenyan version of the talks.

The Joint Commission meeting, which ends on Thursday, will review security and cooperation along the Ethiopia-Kenya border, immigration, refugee affairs and supervision of boundary marks, the television reported.
The commission is composed of Kenyan and Ethiopian central government and provincial administrators and foreign ministry officials from both countries.
Clan attacks across the borders are frequent, with cattle usually the targets, but casualty figures are rarely high.
